skill.name: azure-deploy
skill.description: Deploy validated Azure applications using azd, Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, and CI/CD recipes. The skill checks prerequisites, runs deployment workflows, verifies endpoints, and guides post-deployment fixes.
skill.summary: Run validated Azure deployment workflows with preflight checks, RBAC verification, and post-deployment guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Azure deployment workflow, but it intentionally runs local and Azure CLI commands that can provision or modify cloud resources. I confirmed real risks around shell evaluation, command substitution, curl-to-shell installation, shell scripts, network verification, and elevated SQL or registry credential handling. Many Markdown links, code fences, environment variable references, and .azure deployment-plan references are false positives.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell guidance with a package manager, setup action, or downloaded installer with checksum verification and user confirmation.

remediation.issue: AZD environment output is loaded with eval in shell examples.
remediation.suggestion: Use a safe parser for azd env get-values, validate variable names, and quote values instead of evaluating shell text.

remediation.issue: Runtime managed identities receive persistent db_ddladmin permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Use a separate migration identity for schema changes, then grant runtime identities only the roles required after deployment.

remediation.issue: ACR admin credentials are retrieved and passed to docker login.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Azure AD based az acr login or managed identity flows, and avoid placing passwords in command arguments.

remediation.issue: Deployment commands can modify subscriptions and incur costs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit user confirmation for subscription, region, destructive choices, and any operation that changes RBAC or provisions resources.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe eval of AZD environment output
semantic_findings.description: Several deployment recipes use eval on azd environment output. If an environment value contains shell syntax, the shell can execute unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly show eval applied to azd env get-values output. The risk depends on environment value control, but the unsafe shell pattern is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Broad SQL DDL permissions for runtime identities
semantic_findings.description: The SQL managed identity guidance grants db_datareader, db_datawriter, and db_ddladmin to application identities. Persistent DDL permission lets the app alter or drop schema objects.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The role grants are explicit and repeated in scripts and documentation. They are useful for migrations but exceed least privilege for normal runtime access.

semantic_findings.title: Fallback path exposes ACR admin credentials
semantic_findings.description: The error recovery guide retrieves ACR admin username and password, then passes the password to docker login. This can expose registry credentials through shell history or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands directly retrieve registry credentials and use the password in a CLI argument. The file labels it a fallback, but the exposure path is concrete.

content.value_statement: Azure releases fail when plans, regions, RBAC, and environment settings are not verified. This skill guides validated deployments with Azure CLI, azd, Terraform, and Bicep workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs deployment recipes for prepared Azure projects that already passed validation.
Checks subscriptions, regions, resource groups, and AZD environment settings before deployment.
Guides azd, Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps deployment paths.
Verifies Container Apps and ACR RBAC propagation before switching to deployed images.
Provides post-deployment steps for SQL managed identity access, EF migrations, and endpoint checks.
limitations: Requires an existing validated deployment plan and prepared infrastructure files.
Does not create new applications or scaffold infrastructure from scratch.
Can modify cloud resources and may create costs in the selected Azure subscription.
Requires installed Azure tooling, valid credentials, and user confirmation for destructive choices.

use_cases.title: Release a validated web app
use_cases.description: Deploy an application that already has azure.yaml, infrastructure files, and a validated deployment plan.

use_cases.title: Manage production deployment gates
use_cases.description: Confirm subscription, region, RBAC, and environment settings before running cloud-changing commands.

use_cases.title: Recover failed Azure deployments
use_cases.description: Use targeted recipes to fix RBAC delays, missing environment values, SQL access, and endpoint verification.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy validated project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner deployment from a prepared project
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this validated Azure project. Confirm the subscription and region, then run the required deployment workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy application updates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate update to existing Azure infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy only the application changes for this prepared Azure project. Verify the endpoint URLs after deployment completes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Container Apps deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced two-phase Container Apps and ACR deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this Container Apps project with the ACR RBAC propagation check between provisioning and application deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy with SQL post-configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced deployment with managed identity and migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy the validated project, configure SQL managed identity access, apply EF migrations, and verify the application endpoints.

output_examples.input: Deploy this validated project to Azure.
output_examples.output: Reports the selected subscription and region, completes pre-deploy checks, runs deployment commands, verifies endpoints, and lists follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: The Container App cannot pull from ACR after deployment.
output_examples.output: Identifies the likely RBAC propagation issue, checks the AcrPull assignment, waits for propagation, and recommends retry steps.
Guides managed identity SQL access, migration execution, and database connectivity verification without exposing credentials.

best_practices: Run this skill only after azure-prepare and azure-validate have completed successfully.
Show the user the exact subscription, region, and destructive choices before making cloud changes.
Stream deployment output and record endpoint URLs, RBAC checks, and post-deployment results.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create a new application or generate new infrastructure.
Do not run azd up before confirming subscription, region, and resource group conflicts.
Do not bypass RBAC propagation checks for Container Apps that pull images from ACR.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after preparation and validation are complete, and the project is ready for Azure deployment.

faq.question: Can it create a new Azure application?
faq.answer: No. It deploys prepared applications and refers new app creation to the preparation workflow.

faq.question: Which deployment tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Developer CLI, Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps examples.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The deployment commands require authenticated Azure access with permissions for the selected resources.

faq.question: How does it handle destructive actions?
faq.answer: It requires explicit user confirmation before deletion, overwrites, costly changes, and security-sensitive changes.

faq.question: What happens after deployment?
faq.answer: It verifies service endpoints, checks RBAC status, guides SQL or migration steps, and reports final URLs.
